section_title: Press release: Fremont PD achieves CALEA accreditation
text: City of Fremont press release, August 12, 2026: the Fremont Police Department received Law Enforcement Accreditation from the Commission on Accreditation for Law Enforcement Agencies (CALEA), following nearly two years of work led by Deputy Chief Lance Brede. FPD is among roughly 5% of police agencies worldwide — and six municipal agencies statewide — to earn CALEA accreditation, which the release describes as the gold standard in public safety accreditation, requiring rigorous self-assessment, community engagement, and external review. City and Police leadership testified before the Commission in Omaha, Nebraska in July. Accreditation is ongoing every four years with annual proofs of compliance. Contacts: Amy Gee, FPD Public Affairs, 510-790-6967; Geneva Bosques, City of Fremont, 510-284-4094.

City of Fremont press release, May 19, 2026: the 2026 Point in Time Count identified 852 individuals experiencing homelessness in Fremont, compared to 807 in January 2024 and 1,026 in 2022. The count took place the morning of January 22, 2026, with 106 volunteers. The City credits its Housing Navigation Center, Winter Relief, Keep Fremont Housed, local shelters, and Mobile Evaluation Team programs, under the Homelessness Response Plan adopted in 2024. In South Alameda County overall (Fremont, Newark, Union City), the total decreased by 10. The release notes recent encampment resolutions at Vallejo Mill Park and Isherwood Park with all impacted individuals offered shelter, and the upcoming Natalie's Place shelter in South Fremont.

section_title: Press release: Real Time Information Center opens
text: City of Fremont press release, April 28, 2026: the Fremont Police Department opened its Real Time Information Center (RTIC) facility — a centralized hub using video feeds, license plate reader data, regional law enforcement databases, and public data sources to support real-time decision-making. It is staffed by two specialized analysts, following an initial rollout in May 2025. The RTIC already supported major investigations including an armed retail robbery of a local jeweler. Development was funded by a $2.45 million Organized Retail Theft Prevention grant from the Board of State and Community Corrections. The release states the RTIC operates under strict privacy protections and civil liberties standards.

section_title: Press release: Floyd Mitchell appointed Police Chief
text: City of Fremont press release, March 3, 2026: City Manager Karena Shackelford appointed Floyd Mitchell as Fremont's next Police Chief, effective March 9, 2026, following a nationwide search. Mitchell served 25 years with the Kansas City, Missouri Police Department (rising to Major), then as Police Chief in Temple, Texas; Lubbock, Texas (2019–2023); and Oakland, California, where the city saw decreases in almost all crime categories including a 31% reduction in homicides. He succeeds Sean Washington, who retired August 2025 after 28 years with FPD; Deputy Chief Lance Brede served as interim chief March 4–8, 2026.

section_title: Press release: LS Power grid and broadband MOU
text: City of Fremont press release, December 4, 2025: the City signed a memorandum of understanding with LS Power Grid California for the Newark to Northern Receiving Station 230 kV "Power the South Bay" transmission project — a 12-mile line adding 1 gigawatt of transmission capacity in southern Alameda County, enough to service approximately 600,000 single-family homes. As part of the agreement, LS Power will install and dedicate about six miles of high-capacity broadband conduit to the City, advancing Fremont's Fiber Optic Master Plan and potential future municipal broadband service. Construction was targeted to begin in early 2026 along Boyce Road, Cushing Parkway, and Fremont Boulevard.

section_title: Press release: Police Chief Sean Washington retires
text: City of Fremont press release, June 17, 2025: Police Chief Sean Washington announced his retirement effective August 9, 2025, after 28 years with the Fremont Police Department, including nearly four years as Chief — Fremont's first African American Police Chief (appointed October 1, 2021). Under his tenure FPD launched an Electric Patrol Vehicle Pilot Program, a Drone as First Responder program, and work toward a Real Time Information Center; he expanded the Police Chief's Community Advisory Board and created a Youth Advisory Board. In January 2025 FPD became the first California law enforcement agency to satisfy all requirements for the IACP Trust Building Campaign.

section_title: Press release: 560 new affordable housing units in 2025
text: City of Fremont press release, May 12, 2025: celebrating 560 new affordable housing units leasing in 2025, including the grand opening of Fremont Family Apartments (54 units at 34320 Fremont Blvd., built with Abode Housing Development on repurposed church parking land) plus Bell Street Gardens (126 units converted from a motel), Osgood North, Osgood South, and Serra Apartments. The City contributed $30.7 million in restricted funds to this year's units plus $34 million allocated for future developments. The release cites the California Association of Realtors: in Q1 2025 only 21% of Bay Area households could afford a median single-family home. Under the 2023–2031 Housing Element and RHNA, Fremont is committed to nearly 13,000 new residential units, over 7,000 affordable, by 2031. Residents can join the City's Affordable Housing Interest List for new unit openings.

section_title: Press release: Bay Street parking lot clean-up statement
text: City of Fremont statement, March 14, 2025: addressing disinformation about a photograph of an abatement notice posted on an abandoned wheelchair, the City stated it conducted a scheduled cleanup March 10, 2025 at the Bay Street parking lot in the Irvington District under Fremont Municipal Code section 10.05.600 (public parking facilities). Advance notice was posted 5 days prior; service providers including the City and Bay Area Community Health conducted outreach beginning February 2025; three unhoused residents were referred to the Housing Navigation Center. The wheelchair was not in use when noticed, was not removed on the 10th, and any removed property is stored 90 days for retrieval. The statement references the City's Encampment Condition Guidelines and Homeless Response Plan.
